title: Tokio Marine boots on ground as it circles IAG and Suncorp
full_text:
Japanese insurer Tokio Marine is understood to have sent representatives to Australia in the past three weeks to carry out further exploratory work for a potential $20bn-plus purchase of one of Australia’s top insurance firms.
It is understood that the Japanese financial group had executives on the ground, meeting with representatives of Insurance Australia Group and Suncorp, along with other industry experts in what was understood to be detailed analysis on the two potential targets and the sector.
Some also suggest QBE or Hollard insurance firms could be in its sights, but the general view is that Tokio Marine is most interested in Suncorp or IAG.
DataRoom reported last month that both IAG and Suncorp were considered potential targets for Tokio Marine in what would be one of the largest transactions in history for the Australian insurance industry at more than $20bn.
DataRoom understands that IAG has Goldman Sachs in its corner for any negotiations, while Suncorp is close to Barrenjoey.
Bank of America would probably be advising Tokio Marine, sources said. It is understood that, as of last month, neither Suncorp nor IAG had received any approaches.
However, it is believed the Japanese suitor wants to embark on a transaction to put excess capital to work, and analysts say it told the market about two months ago it wanted to break into the Australian or Canadian market with a major acquisition.
Founded in 1879, Tokio Marine is a global insurer operating in more than 50 countries and regions with more than 50,000 employees worldwide.
Insurers globally are reaping a windfall from inflation-fuelled price increases, justified partly by the threat of catastrophic events brought on by climate change.
As a result, they have recorded near-record profits and prospered on the back of higher interest rates, as their cash holdings generate more earnings. Normally, Tokio Marine would target a specialty insurer focused on commercial lines, such as QBE, but it appears to be casting its net more broadly this time.
